top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) is the best-defended outcome: the magic-wavelength condition was a quantitative prediction that was verified, 10^-18 uncertainties have been reproduced and intercompared across independent laboratories with Sr, Yb and Hg, and the credit is the least disputed on the list. The citation is tied to the magic-wavelength lattice, which separates it from the 2005 and 2012 timekeeping prizes. Residual concerns are the priority record (Lemonde, Takamoto and others) and the refinement-versus-discovery question. P002 (hexatic melting) is a clean three-name theory credit but is system dependent experimentally and overlaps with the 2016 prize, so I rank it second. A real award on a sound discovery is preferable to no award, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I am a theoretical condensed-matter physicist, close to the twisted bilayer graphene field (not on the slate), with no known connection to Katori, Ye, Halperin, Nelson or Young.
